bugs.text: Enemies are created in state 'wait' and nothing ever moves them to 'entering'; they are never drawn, never fly in, never fire, never dive and can't be hit. Every normal stage is an empty playfield forever (confirmed by all play screenshots).
Stage can never be cleared because the 40 invisible 'wait' enemies are never removed: endless soft-lock on stage 1 with no way to score, die or reach game over.

Challenging stage: waves have no startAt and no escaped field, so no enemy ever spawns and the stage never finishes (soft-lock); chHits is never incremented, so NUMBER OF HITS and PERFECT are always wrong.
Tractor beam can never start: it requires the boss to already hold a captive, which can only come from a beam capture; startCaptiveDive is never called.
fireAt stores plain numbers but is read as {at, done}; entering and diving enemies never fire.
Game over sets overT=0 before entering 'over', so the GAME OVER / results screen lasts one frame before returning to title.
Formation shots play the enemy-hit sound.
First hit on a Boss shows a '150' popup without awarding points.
Dual fighter hit always drops the same (red/right) half regardless of which half was hit.
Stage badges cycle one flag per stage instead of the arcade's denomination sums.

summary: The file is tidy on the surface: a correct fixed-timestep loop, crisp 224x288 integer scaling, a good twinkling starfield, a clean HUD and title screen, readable sectioned code and a full set of synthesized sounds. But the core is dead: enemies are created in a 'wait' state that nothing ever advances, so after STAGE 1 the player flies alone on an empty screen forever. Nothing can be shot, nothing shoots back, the stage never ends, and game over, the results screen, the extra ship and the high-score save are all unreachable. Several other systems would fail even if that were fixed: the tractor beam needs a captive to start, so it can never start; challenge waves have no start time and never spawn; dive and entry firing use the wrong data shape; and the game-over screen would last one frame. In practice this is a starfield with a movable ship, nothing like Galaga.
